cand.title: 51st Annual IAEA Conference
cand.excerpt: September 27–October 2, 2026 Toronto conference with international delegates, visa-support documentation and negotiated room blocks at the conference venue and nearby hotels. This is the strongest verified lodging-demand prospect in the set, with a multi-night international delegate pattern and concurrent meeting/catering potential.

findings.namedBuyers: Nick Ferraro and Arbana Miftari are explicitly identified by the association as IAEA 2026 Conference Managers. They are relevant operational contacts for a post-event housing review and referral to any later Toronto requirements, not verified contracting authorities or confirmed 2027 managers. The published shared conference route is info@iaea2026.org; it is not a personal email. Dan Koenig, EQAO CEO, is the named local host executive and a senior relationship/sponsor route, not a proven housing buyer. The association contact page lists Anne Oberholzer as IAEA Secretary; use as a series-governance referral route, with currency of that undated listing to be checked.
findings.futureEdition: The 51st edition ended October 2, 2026 and is already past as of November 15, 2026. The next officially announced edition is the 52nd Annual IAEA Conference, October 3–8, 2027, Grand Hotel Palace, Thessaloniki, Central Macedonia, Greece. The association announcement was published October 25, 2026; October 3–8 are activity dates, not publication dates. This falls within the requested horizon but is not a Toronto opportunity. No official 2028 edition announcement was located; do not extrapolate dates or a Toronto return.
findings.hotelProductFit: Assessment using the supplied hotel specifications: this is a city-conference/urban lodging fit, not inherently a resort lead. Toronto 2026 had 400 actual attendees from 40 countries, with multi-hotel accommodation. A 157-room Radisson Blu and approximately 240-theatre largest room cannot be positioned as exclusive housing and full-conference plenary venue for that historical scale. Conditional future roles are a modest delegate/speaker room block, executive lodging or smaller side meetings, only if a Toronto event is announced and the buyer requests them. No 15–109-room demand is evidenced for this event. The hotel’s proximity to MTCC is not a demand driver for a conference at Eaton Centre, and no Harbourfront demand is documented. Do not promise catering or restaurant/lounge service without hotel-side verification. The 2025 resort venue shows resort hosting has occurred, not that the series requires resorts.
findings.venueCommitments: 2026 historical venue: Marriott Downtown at CF Toronto Eaton Centre, 525 Bay Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5G 2L2, Canada. It is in Toronto proper, downtown/Eaton Centre, not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. The host explicitly published a reserved delegate room block there. 2027 announced venue: Grand Hotel Palace, Monastiriou 305, Thessaloniki, Central Macedonia, Greece, 54628; entirely outside Toronto. The official announcement establishes the venue, not disclosure of a signed contract, room allocation or exclusive housing arrangement.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified sequence: 49th edition, September 22–25, 2024, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States, hosted by ETS; exact venue not established in the reviewed primary page. 50th edition, September 21–26, 2025, Avani Victoria Falls Resort, Livingstone, Zambia, hosted by the Examinations Council of Zambia. The 2025 brochure distinguishes arrivals September 21, workshops September 22, core conference September 23–25 and excursion September 26; an older association announcement used September 23–26. 51st edition, September 27–October 2, 2026, Toronto Marriott, hosted by EQAO with Vretta support. 52nd edition announced for October 3–8, 2027 in Thessaloniki. These are published editions, not an inferred annual calendar. Toronto was the first Canadian host in 2026; no fixed Canadian return cycle is established.
findings.accommodationSourcing: 2026 edition-specific organizer-negotiated blocks with hotel booking links, including the venue hotel and nearby hotels; no named official housing bureau or open hotel RFP was located. FAQ quote: “We have negotiated a discounted rate for a block of rooms at the conference venue hotel and additional hotels nearby.” It adds that “there are only a limited number of rooms blocked”. Every distinct hotel listed: Marriott Downtown at CF Toronto Eaton Centre; Hyatt Regency; Yonge Suites Apartment Hotel; Toor Hotel (by Hyatt); Chelsea Hotel; Cambridge Suites; Courtyard by Marriott Toronto Downtown; Hampton Inn & Suites (by Hilton); Holiday Inn Express; Holiday Inn. Most negotiated rates are marked expired; the Hyatt Regency entry gives September 27, 2026 as its validity deadline. These are historical arrangements, not currently available inventory. 2027: Grand Hotel Palace is the announced conference venue; housing bureau, delegate rates, booking process, room-block commitment and additional hotels are not established in the announcement, which says the conference website will launch soon. Hotel sourcing must not be marked open.
findings.organizationStructure: Event series owner: International Association for Educational Assessment, a professional international assessment association, not the International Atomic Energy Agency. The 2026 local host was the Education Quality and Accountability Office (EQAO), a board-governed agency of Ontario’s Ministry of Education. Vretta, a digital assessment and learning-solutions company, was the supporting partner. Marriott was the conference venue/host hotel, not the event owner. No external PCO, DMC or housing bureau was identified in the reviewed edition materials; do not label Vretta a PCO or assume it controlled hotel contracts. The 2027 announcement does not name the local host or housing buyer.
findings.competitiveLimitations: 2026 lodging was already marketed through ten named hotels; Radisson Blu was not listed. The Marriott held the conference and a delegate block, creating an incumbent convenience advantage. The published nearby blocks establish distributed accommodation, but neither their limited size nor multiple hotels proves sellout, unmet demand, displacement or unsatisfied overflow. No room-block counts, pickup, peak rooms or room-nights were found. For 2027 the decisive barrier is Thessaloniki geography; Grand Hotel Palace is a hotel venue, but its designation alone does not establish an exclusive accommodation contract.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Remove the 51st edition from active-date Toronto sales qualification and record the 52nd edition separately as confirmed in Thessaloniki. Send one short post-event introduction via info@iaea2026.org for Nick Ferraro and Arbana Miftari: ask who managed the 2026 room blocks, whether any accommodation gaps actually occurred, and whether there are separately scheduled Toronto follow-on meetings or a published return-hosting process. Offer a small-room-block/side-meeting discussion only if such local needs are confirmed; do not send a speculative 2027 Toronto accommodation bid. Ask for a series-secretariat referral if appropriate. Verify catering capability before offering a hosted reception.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: No remaining 2026 edition accessibility: September 27–October 2, 2026 is historical and predates the December 6, 2026 horizon opening. The next confirmed edition is in Greece, not Toronto. There is therefore no verified in-horizon Toronto room or meeting opportunity from this event. Residual 2026 booking links must not be treated as live sourcing.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference/strategy only: retain a low-priority relationship with the 2026 organizing team and request notice of a genuinely announced Toronto/Canada return or separate local meeting. Published international rotation supports a recurring series, not recurring Toronto demand. Do not assign future room revenue, a 2028 date, an open RFP, or an anticipated Toronto cycle. The known 2027 venue is not contestable Toronto lodging demand.
